intent: The menu row that opens its MenubarSub's popup beside it.
typical_uses: A row such as Share or Move to that leads to a nested list

dont_use_when.situation: A row that runs an action when chosen

invariants.text: While `openOnHover` is on, which it is unless set to false, a mouse pointer resting on the row opens the submenu after `delay` milliseconds (100 when not given) and leaving closes it after `closeDelay` milliseconds (0 when not given); with `openOnHover` false, pressing the row toggles the submenu instead.
The row always ends in a right-pointing chevron; there is no prop to leave it out, and it does not mirror in a right-to-left layout.
dropdown-menu.module.css keeps the row highlighted while its submenu is open.

dropdown-menu.module.css sizes every descendant `svg` of the row to the small icon size and keeps it from shrinking or taking pointer events, so a leading icon passed in children needs no size of its own.

anti_patterns.dont: Give the row an `onClick` that runs an action
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep the action on a MenubarItem inside the submenu; the row's job is to open the submenu, so an action on it fires when the user only meant to look inside

a11y.by: the primitive's Menu.SubmenuTrigger renders role="menuitem"; menubar.test.tsx asserts the row is found by the menuitem role and name 'Share' and that clicking it opens the submenu's items

onClick.states: onClick is a callback called with the click event when the row is pressed
onClick.because: A React event handler - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the sub-trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the sub-trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, highlighted, open). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dropdown-menu.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Rendered by MenubarSubTrigger after the children; the kit exposes no prop to replace or hide it.

good.title: A sub-trigger with a leading icon

bad.title: A sub-trigger outside any MenubarSub
bad.why: The row has no submenu to open; place it with a MenubarSubContent inside a MenubarSub.

onClick.description: TS: ((event: BaseUIEvent<MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement, MouseEvent>>) => void) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. onClick is a callback called with the click event when the row is pressed. A React event handler - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.
